extracted.intended_audience: general readers and fans of late-night comedy (encyclopedia audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and describe recurring sketch types, comedic techniques, and features used on Late Night with Conan O'Brien (character bits, visual gags, parody formats, running jokes, timing devices, etc.). Useful for understanding how recurring late-night bits create humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pointless zany randomness (payoff required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Will not waste the audience's time with zany, random jokes, only to introduce a completely zany, random character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jokes or bizarre elements should have payoff or context; random surreal elements without setup can feel like wasted time. Example critique: do not insert an unrelated zany character with no connection to the bit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorable recurring characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of distinctive, repeatable characters (e.g., Masturbating Bear, Pierre Bernard, Triumph the Insult Comic Dog) that can be brought back in different contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters should have clear, repeatable traits and hooks that make successive appearances recognizable and funny; can be retooled for different time slots or audiences (e.g., reintroducing late-night-inappropriate characters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadpan / dry delivery contrasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor arises from delivering outrageous content in a soft-spoken, disarmingly calm, or emotionless voice (Pierre Bernard's 'recliner of rage' example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast between extreme content and understated delivery heightens absurdity. Example: long drawn-out rants about niche interests spoken calmly create comedic tension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-based niche-rant structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A performer sits (recliner) and delivers a long, focused rant about a niche interest, culminating in a punchline/ask ("Bottom line, America...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustained specificity and an expected closing line provide rhythm and payoff; the niche specificity invites recognition from a sub-audience and adds character credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of puppets for gross-out/subversive humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Puppets are used to say or do shocking, obscene, or taboo things (Vomiting Kermit; puppet exclaiming being born with both sets of genitalia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Puppets' assumed innocence amplifies transgressive jokes; juxtapose puppet form with adult content for shock/comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-media / crossover character appearances
rubrics_metrics.description: A puppet or character may cross over to other shows or be retrieved ceremonially (Triumph crossing over to The Tonight Show, Conan retrieving Triumph from Fallon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recurring characters can be leveraged across platforms/shows for meta-humor and to reward long-term viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-budget visual technique (Syncro-Vox) as comedic device
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Syncro-Vox (a still image with superimposed live-moving mouth) to create fake celebrity interviews and visual incongruity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low-budget aesthetic is part of the joke; pairing a cheap visual effect with biting impersonations heightens the absurdity of the faux-interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impersonation and lampooning of real celebrities
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent impersonations of well-known public figures exaggerating perceived traits (e.g., Trump saying 'you're fired!' and 'yuge').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select recognizable mannerisms and topical catchphrases; exaggeration should be clearly linked to public image for audience recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slapstick / physical-prop gags
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical sight gags using props/puppets, such as a robot on a toilet making clanging noises and raising arms in celebration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple physical premises with timed sound effects or visual surprise work well in a studio context; build to a visible payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical satire via familiar formats (SAT Analogies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a familiar testing/quiz format to satirize current events or celebrities (satirized SAT analogies based on current events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mimicking recognizable formats gives structure; update content with current references for immediacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal/animal-character gross-out for shock laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals used for unexpected gross or shocking behavior (Quackers the duck defecating and rubbing beak as if eating it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shock from animal misbehavior can elicit strong audience reaction; use carefully for comedic timing and shock value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Out-of-context clip juxtaposition via a prop (the Lever)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prop (Walker, Texas Ranger lever) that supposedly triggers random clips taken wildly out of context for comedic juxtaposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Juxtaposition of unrelated footage with a host reaction produces humor; a repeated 'one last time' escalation gag enhances payoff. Beware legal/IP concerns when using real clips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation and 'one last time' gag structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A sketch ends but immediately resumes for an additional, often more absurd repeat (pulling the lever 'one last time').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the false ending to surprise audience expectation; each additional repeat should escalate the absurdity or shock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider/niche-reference humor (nerding for Pierre)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explaining news stories by relating them to obscure anime/sci-fi references that only the niche character understands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mismatched knowledge domains create humor; reward viewers who recognize references while making the mismatch itself the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation subversion in audience Q&A
rubrics_metrics.description: Host invites audience questions about career but receives banal or obscure questions (how to grow a plant), producing disappointment and a host's expert answer on niche topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up audience expectation and then intentionally subvert it; the host's unexpected expertise compounds the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parody of genre using extreme constraint (e.g., '60' parody of 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parody the structure of a serious format by exaggerating its constraints (one-second episodes representing a single minute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the original format's signature devices and amplify them to absurdity; structural constraints can be the core joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exaggerated character arcs (child crush to homicidal rage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Take a small, relatable emotion (a crush) and escalate it to extreme, incongruous reactions for humor (adorable bashfulness to volcanic, homicidal rage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exaggeration of emotional scale and unpredictability makes character bits memorable; maintain comedic timing when escalating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antiquated-style parody with offensive lyrical content (Artie Kendall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an old-fashioned musical style to present anachronistic or offensive views, with repeated melody and changing topical lyrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contrast between upbeat vintage style and problematic lyrics creates discomfort-based humor; repeated melody anchors the bit across variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staged 'random' celebrity audience members
rubrics_metrics.description: Host picks a 'random' audience member who is actually a celebrity planted in the crowd to create surprise reveals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Element of surprise plus the celebrity's recognition of being 'found' functions as the gag; placement and timing are key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fake-talent audience bits (anti-climax reveals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present audience members with 'unique talents' that are obviously faked, generating anti-climax humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build expectation for a talent reveal then invert with deliberately ridiculous or fake performance for laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parody/pastiche of children's cartoons with adult humor (Conan Babies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mimic the look and tropes of children’s cartoons (limited animation, theme song) but populate with adult or absurd content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain recognizable genre markers while inserting adult-incongruous content to produce layered humor accessible to multiple audience segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voiceover diary for dramatic irony
rubrics_metrics.description: Host writes in a diary with onstage voiceover revealing private, often insulting thoughts about the guest (Conan's 'Hello Kitty' diary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dramatic irony (audience hears host's inner thoughts) produces cringe and laughter; keep voiceover concise and sharply observational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soothing form contrasted with horrific content (lullaby bit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a gentle format (a lullaby) to recite disturbing or adult material, then flip to an explicit punchline (telling parents to have sex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast between tone and content is the engine of the joke; escalate gradually and then deliver blunt inversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition and formula parody (boy band parody)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parody formulaic pop groups by repeating trademark words and phrases (e.g., 'awesome' 28 times) and creating a deliberately bad song.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counting repetition or intentional banality highlights the source material's clichés; exaggerate to absurd extremes for comedic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dead/recorded guests and mechanical malfunctions (mannequin emergency guest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use prerecorded or mechanical guests (mannequin in emergency box) whose glitches create awkward, surreal interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controlled malfunction timing is important; the host's attempts to maintain normalcy are part of the humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stereotype/caricature sketches (European smugness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a caricatured national type to satirize attitudes (smug European superiority, odd clothing and products).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters should exaggerate mannerisms and cultural tropes for clear contrast; beware of relying on lazy harmful stereotypes without satirical purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring celebrity cameo gags (Friends of the Show)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invite the same celebrities repeatedly in bizarre situations to build an internal running gag (Mr. T, Abe Vigoda, James Lipton).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarity and predictable roles allow the audience to anticipate and relish subversions; keep cameo usage fresh with new contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shock-reveal costume gag (Fun Hole Guy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with a normal-looking character who reveals an unexpected, shocking costume element (man in sweater reveals fishnets and 'Fun Hole' shirt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The timing of the reveal and the audience's escalating discomfort are central; this relies on the contrast between expectation and final image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irreverent escalation to religious figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use religious archetypes (Good Priest/Bad Priest, calling in Jesus/Mary/Joseph) then escalate to irreverent or absurd outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Play with sacred tropes to create taboo humor while balancing with clear comedic intent to avoid gratuitous offense (and to achieve a punchline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirical mockery of celebrity scandals (Guest Autographs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show fictitious guest autographs that parody tabloid stories or current scandals to mock celebrities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie the forged autograph message to an existing public scandal for immediacy; audience recognition of the target is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absurd situational parody (Instant Audience Member Upgrade)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply an everyday service parody (airline upgrades) to a show-specific context (audience seating) and exaggerate benefits for humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map a familiar institutional ritual to an improbable context and escalate the absurdity of perks and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trope-subversion with unexpected guardian (devil + bear)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of the expected angel vs. devil moral trope, substitute an unexpected figure (bear) who gives off-topic advice, flipping the expected moral debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subverting established tropes by replacing elements with incongruous ones creates novelty; ensure the substitute has its own consistent (comic) logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetitive death/escape montage with stock footage
rubrics_metrics.description: A character repeatedly declares 'no reason to live' then departs via increasingly ridiculous transport using stock footage matches (kayak down a mountain, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cutting between studio action and stock footage for comedic mismatch depends on precise editing and timing; repetition across iterations builds the gag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive-pattern image puzzles with punchline
rubrics_metrics.description: Show a series of images linked by a progressive pattern leading to a wordplay punchline (Squirrel → handyman → insane asylum → Tom Green → 'missing a nut').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up a clear pattern and then land a witty or punning conclusion; pacing of reveals matters to audience comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mashup archetypes with rhyming character voices (Pimpbot 5000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine incongruous archetypes (1950s robot + 1970s pimp) and express them in a stylized, rhyming speech pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The novelty comes from the unlikely combination and a consistent voice (rhymes and catchphrases) that reinforces the mashup identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta/corporate self-satire (pleasing affiliates, Polly Peacock)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make jokes about the network or corporate relationships by personifying the logo or addressing affiliate needs in absurd ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-referential mockery can defuse corporate constraints and generate insider laughs; exaggerate promotional language into absurd claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring-character motif with theme song/hook (Preparation H Raymond)
rubrics_metrics.description: A costumed character distributes a branded product while singing a recurring theme; topical jokes are woven into repeated structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A simple repeated hook (song line, catchphrase) anchors the recurring bit and allows topical updates within a familiar frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surreal non sequitur sign-off language (Queen Elizabeth Calls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrity/royal calls go off-topic and end comments by addressing the host with random bisyllabic words (Coughdrop O'Branflakes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventive malapropisms or non sequiturs as sign-offs create an absurd signature and can be returned to for continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive camera exaggeration of an audience distractor
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeatedly cut to an audience member, each cut more exaggerated with visual/audio effects, culminating in an over-the-top reveal that disrupts the show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Escalation of attention and effects must be rhythmically timed; the final reveal should justify the buildup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invented-channel sketch (Satellite TV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invent fake TV channels with absurd premises to parody cable/satellite lineups (e.g., 'Jar Barf', 'Men Without Hats Channel').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a list of channel concepts that each satirize a real TV trope; quick sketches or clips for each channel maintain pace and variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical parody combined with physical gag (The Slipnutz)
rubrics_metrics.description: A musical act whose entire routine is a physical gag (slipping on nuts) paired with a deliberately goofy theme song.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Musical parody works when the song plays straight while the physical gag subverts performance expectations; repeatable bits can evolve (opening for Slipknot).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta 'spoiler alert' gag to satirize censorship culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a visible, physical 'spoiler alert' (people covering their ears and yelling) to humorously 'protect' viewers from spoilers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exaggerated physical censorship as commentary on spoiler culture; the gag's absurdity depends on audience familiarity with 'spoiler' norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period-piece traveling-salesman archetype
rubrics_metrics.description: Play a 1950s-style traveling salesman with anachronistic voice and scripted sales pitch to sell unfunny jokes or useless products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchoring the character in a recognizable historical archetype allows lampooning of old-timey tropes; consistent vocal choices and catchphrases strengthen the gag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grotesque/incongruous mascot satire (Unknown Colleges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invent mascots that are grotesque, unrelated, or in poor taste to mock institutional mascots (e.g., S&M Lincoln).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The humor depends on the shock of mismatch and transgression; sensitive subjects risk alienating viewers if not clearly framed as satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zoom-out reveal progression (What in the World?)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show an extreme close-up then progressively zoom out to reveal an initially mundane object which then yields an unexpected outrageous element off-frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pacing of zoom-outs and the timing of guesses are crucial; the final reveal must be surprising but logically connected to earlier frames.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasonal/annual event parody and stunts
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce special recurring bits tied to annual events (State of the Show Address parodying State of the Union; Central Time Zone New Year's Countdown; World's Fastest Menorah holiday gag).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time bits to coincide with real calendar events for topical resonance; recurring annual elements build tradition and viewer anticipation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of hidden mechanics for visual gags (menorah on hidden platform)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a visual gag that appears to defy physics (menorah flying by via hidden platform) accompanied by recognizable music cues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain secrecy of the mechanic for the illusion; pair with cultural music for immediate recognition (e.g., 'Hava Nagila').
